name: Tilted landmarks
slug: Cardinal cave carvings set a few degrees off true bearing
description: Four landscape carvings in the roost cave show the largest landmark to the east, west, north, and south, each a mountain or an island, as seen from the ruined tower. Each is a small number of degrees off the cardinal bearing where it should sit. The western one is drawn like a clock hand that has slipped from nine o'clock toward nine-twenty or nine-thirty.

log.summary: Elrus cannot make the angles fit a single vantage and attributes them to Grixto carving from a faulty memory. Walker believes matching the real landscape to that tilt will point toward a place to go or a thing to find. An investigation from the tower was called and not resolved.
